archetype: A mono-red critical-mass copy engine wearing an aggro costume. deck-audit matches it to `aggro` from strategic_frame.json and the creature count agrees (27, inside 26-32), but the frame's reading is the right one: the 1/1s are not the clock, they are Zada's copy multiplier, Skirk Prospector's mana and Skullclamp's fuel. Two half-decks share the 99 — a commander-gated copy engine and a storm half — and only the first is gated at the level `goldfish_targets.json` declares. Individual cards in the second half still read the command zone: Siege-Gang Lieutenant's Lieutenant clause needs you to control your commander, and War Room prices its draw off commander colour identity.
verdict: This deck functions and it builds: the mana base is at every target, the turn-3 land drop lands 90% of the time, and five stacks are checker-passed. Read the gating before the prescription. Of the three declared targets only `Zada online with a cantrip drawn` is `commander_gated: true`; `Early token maker drawn` and `Storm payoff plus ritual drawn` are both false. Of the five passing stacks only 001 and 003 put Zada on the board — 002 resolves off Impact Tremors and four Mountains, 005 off Storm-Kiln Artist and three tokens, and 004 states in its own extras that she is in the command zone. So the storm half, including the Storm-Kiln Artist + Haze of Rage line that drives the bracket-4 floor, does not need her. What is limited is the half that carries the deck: the 66.1%-assembling plan and the only checker-passed kill (003) both need one 3/3 to survive the turn you commit, and the deck holds exactly one card that helps — Swiftfoot Boots, since Roaming Throne's Ward {2} is on Roaming Throne.

gaps: No `deck_recon.json` exists for this deck, so nothing here is grounded in what strong Zada lists actually run — there are no per-commander inclusion rates in any artifact in this repo. Every add is argued from this deck's own measurements. Settled by a `deck-recon` pass.

Goldfish models resource development only — no removal, no interaction. Nothing measures how often Zada actually survives to the pivot turn, so the protection finding is an argument from card counts, gating flags and the corpus, not a simulated rate.

`Chaos Warp` has no entry in `card_roles.json`, so the deck's only catch-all answer is invisible to `interaction` and `interaction-breadth`. Same class of miss: `Daring Discovery`, `Spreading Insurrection`, `Fists of Flame` and `Wild Ride` are all unclassified.

strategic_frame.json lists 'No storm/critical-mass theory section' and 'No commander-protection/insurance section' among its gaps. Both now exist — `strategy:critical-mass.storm-math` and `strategy:multiplayer.commander-insurance` — and are cited here, so the frame's gap list is stale on those two entries.

strategic_frame.json names Great Train Heist among Zada's cantrips. Its three Spree modes untap your creatures, pump your team, or choose target opponent — none of them targets a creature, so the copy trigger cannot fire on it. Worth a re-check of that engine line; it is a card read, not a rules ruling.

The corpus has no section on a commander whose own ability requires you to target it. `strategy:multiplayer.commander-insurance` recommends boots-style constant protection without that caveat, and the Lightning Greaves reading here — shroud blocks your own cantrip, but equip {0} lets you move it off on your main phase, so the real cost is confined to the pivot turn — is read off the cards, not cited. Settled by a `research-strategy` pass.

The bench holds one card (Sazacap's Brew) and strategic_frame.json records why it is not a Zada enabler: it targets a player, so the copy trigger never fires. There is effectively no sideboard to draw on.

findings.note: "mean bodies is 2.698 on turn 4 ... so an early cantrip copies fewer than twice" inverts its own figure. Zada copies "for each OTHER creature you control", and goldfish_metrics' mean_bodies_by_turn already excludes her: goldfish.py:build_library drops commanders from the library, and bodies_cum only accumulates cards cast out of hand, so the commander is never a body. 2.698 is therefore 2.698 OTHER creatures and a cantrip cast on turn 4 makes ~2.7 copies, i.e. MORE than twice. Corroborated arithmetically inside the artifact: turn 3 is 2.355 and turn 4 is 2.698, a rise of 0.343 — smaller than the 0.7002 the commander alone would contribute if she were counted (cast_turn_histogram['4'] = 7002). The 27-creature count, the 26-32 band and the 7,002 figure are all correct; only the inference is wrong.

Restates the axes[10] error as the justification for the add: "Mean bodies on turn 4 ... is 2.698, so the first cantrip copies fewer than twice." Same evidence as above (goldfish.py:build_library, mean_bodies_by_turn['3']=2.355 vs ['4']=2.698). Hordeling Outburst may still be a correct add — width before the pivot is real, and the fodder group is 5 per goldfish_targets.json — but the measured premise offered for it says the opposite of what the number says. Note also that conditioning on the 7,002 runs where she lands ON turn 4 is not what 2.698 measures; that conditional mean is unmeasured by any artifact here and would need a goldfish pass, not an assertion.

"nothing in the corpus conditions a protection count on how much of the deck routes through the command zone" reaches past the corpus. Three places condition exactly that, two of them sections this document already cites: (1) the interaction-suite band it quotes verbatim in the same entry runs "2-4 protection generic, 4-6 combo, 6-8 Voltron" — Voltron IS the maximally commander-routed archetype and carries the highest count; (2) strategy:deckbuilding.archetype-selection (cited at axes[10] and axes[15]) says "A deck whose only payoff sits in the command zone hands three opponents one target; buy it back with redundant copies ... or protection"; (3) strategy:multiplayer.commander-insurance (cited in this same entry) opens "When the engine routes through your commander, protection is insurance priced against the recast tax" and gives "Cullen's decision test: how critical is the commander to the plan". None of these is a *numeric* test for this deck, which is the narrow sense in which the sentence is defensible — but an unqualified "nothing in the corpus" is doing load-bearing work against the 5-7 figure and the corpus does not support it. Scoping fix, not a reversal: the one-slot arithmetic itself is sound (see the supported finding at axes[8]). lean_into[2] and open_questions[1] state the same idea correctly and narrowly ("the corpus gives no test for that case") — only this sentence over-reaches.

"The one-target enabler class ... 6 cards" equates the class with the goldfish_targets.json any_of group. The group is 6 (verified: Crimson Wisps, Expedite, Renegade Tactics, Ancestors' Aid, Fists of Flame, Wild Ride) but the CLASS is a floor, and this deck's own strategic_frame.json names Witch's Mark among Zada's cantrips — its oracle text is "Create a Wicked Role token attached to up to one target creature you control", so choosing Zada as that one target makes the spell target only Zada and each copy repeats "You may discard a card. If you do, draw two cards." Witch's Mark is in the 99 (audit counts it under card-advantage and threat-density) and is neither counted here nor raised as a candidate, while Daring Discovery — the same situation — IS raised at open_questions[2]. Same overstated size at axes[15] ("any of the six one-target enablers") and lean_into[0] (evidence.size 6, the top prescription in the document). The prescription to deepen the class may survive at 7 or 8 members; the redundancy step it is priced against (31%->41%) does not survive unexamined.

"the only card in the 99 that produces anything off a cast trigger" is false as written. Frontline Heroism is in the 99 and reads "Whenever you cast a spell that targets only a single creature you control, create a 1/1 red Soldier creature token with haste, then copy that spell" — a cast trigger that produces a body and a spell copy. This document names Frontline Heroism itself at lean_into[0]. The component label ("Storm-Kiln Artist — the only cast-triggered MANA source, ungated") is correct and I verified it against every oracle text in the 99: Impulsive Pilferer is on death, Ancestors' Aid on resolution, Fountainport for {4}, Great Train Heist on combat damage, Howlsquad Heavy is an activated tap. Only the word "anything" in the why over-reaches; the SPF itself stands.

"This is the deck's single largest mana battery — four mana from one tap" is contradicted by a card the same document lists as a persistent producer at axes[1]: Howlsquad Heavy, "Max speed — {T}: Add {R} for each Goblin you control". At the deck's own measured board (mean_bodies_by_turn 4.068 on turn 5, 5.257 by turn 6) that tap exceeds four, and Howlsquad's mana is unrestricted where Throne's is "only to cast monocolored spells of that color". The max-speed gate is real and is the honest rescope ("the largest UNCONDITIONAL one-tap battery"), but as written the superlative is unqualified and wrong. Everything else in this entry checks out and I verified it: mean_available_mana_by_turn['6']=5.182, ramp 15 vs 10-12 with six ramp:ritual (mana_analysis.ramp['ramp:ritual']=6), MV histogram mode 2, and the seven colourless nonland cards are exactly the seven named.

closes is "engine component: payoff (storm kill)" and the why calls Reiterate "a third member of the two-card payoff group", citing the redundancy table ("5 copies is 31% of openers, 7 is 41%"). That table prices independent copies of an effect CLASS, and an any_of group's semantics is that any ONE member satisfies the component — but Reiterate satisfies nothing alone. A hand of Reiterate plus a ritual has no storm payoff; "a copied Grapeshot is a Grapeshot" only after Grapeshot is already in hand. So it cannot buy the 2->3 redundancy step the citation is quoted for. What it actually closes is velocity/mana (Reiterate + Mana Geyser, produces "Infinite red mana", "Infinite storm count") — a different component. The contrast is internal: add_candidates[4] gives Birgi an explicit "Not full redundancy" note for a much smaller gap and this entry gives none. Separately verified and SOUND in this entry: I recomputed every combo line in combo_details.json that is one card away from this decklist with the missing card inside mono-red Commander-legal identity (52 deduped lines, 38 distinct pool cards). Reiterate + Mana Geyser at 24,136 is indeed the highest-popularity line whose produces[] is flagged Infinite, and Repercussion + Blasphemous Act at 31,612 is higher but reads "Near-infinite damage to all players". The rescoped superlative holds exactly as written.

Re-grounding verified end to end. The quote is verbatim in strategy:deckbuilding.interaction-suite: "Answers to answers are a separate budget — Commander Deck Maker: 2-4 protection generic, 4-6 combo, 6-8 Voltron; counterspells do both jobs." The 5-7 quote is verbatim in strategy:deckbuilding.threat-density and matches the target deck-audit carries on this axis. The invented premise ("the band is sized for a deck that routes entirely through its commander") is gone from axes[8], lean_into[2] and add_candidates[0] — I grepped all three; what remains at add_candidates[0] is a different over-reach, filed separately. Card reads verified: Roaming Throne's printed line is "Ward {2}" on itself (card_roles.json files it protection:self, which is why the audit counts it); Swiftfoot Boots grants hexproof, which is "your opponents control" only and so does not block your own cantrip. I regexed all 79 main-deck entries for hexproof/shroud/indestructible/protection from/ward/regenerate/prevent damage/counter target and those two are the ONLY hits, so "the only card in the 99 that keeps Zada alive" holds. Shinka grants first strike; Great Train Heist's {2} mode grants +1/+0 and first strike. Arithmetic: 1 effective < 2 (lower floor) and < 5 (upper floor); 1 + 1 = 2 = the lower band's floor exactly. One slot is the figure both bands support. open_questions[1] correctly routes the generic-vs-combo choice to research-strategy — the corpus genuinely gives no test for bracket-4 combo content with a value-engine median.

The probe is engaged rather than dodged. deck-audit's possible_uncounted list is exactly the ten cards named — Crimson Wisps, Expedite, Fists of Flame, Forgotten Cave, Fountainport, Gempalm Incinerator, Idol of Oblivion, Renegade Tactics, Smoldering Crater, War Room — and I confirmed each draws or cycles in its oracle text. The audit reads this axis "under" at 8 vs a floor of 10; the diagnosis reads it "adequate" and says why. Stack 001's final_state records cards_drawn: 5 off one {R} Crimson Wisps, as quoted.

The taxonomy call is right. card_roles.json files Blasphemous Act as ['ramp:cost-reduction', 'removal:damage'] and the audit's sweepers `how` is "copies carrying any of removal:sweeper", so 0 is an artifact of the role vocabulary, not an absence. I scanned all 79 main entries: Blasphemous Act is the only text that damages or destroys every creature (Vandalblast overloaded hits artifacts only). The three free sac outlets are real (Goblin Bombardment any creature, Skirk Prospector a Goblin for {R}, Goblin Trashmaster a Goblin) — minor: Trashmaster's parenthetical "when an opposing artifact exists" is tighter than its text, which can target your own Treasures or Sol Ring, and calling it unconditional in the same breath as conditioning it is internally untidy. Not a defect in the conclusion.

Chaos Warp is genuinely ABSENT from card_roles.json — I looked it up directly, as are Daring Discovery, Spreading Insurrection, Fists of Flame and Wild Ride, exactly as gaps[2] states. The recount is arithmetically consistent with deck-audit's by_class (creature 5, artifact 2, rest 0): Chaos Warp answers any permanent, so 6/3/1/1/0 with graveyard still uncovered.

Every claim about the stacks checks against their final_state blocks, all five checker.verdict == pass. 003: "at least 30 (32 power minus at most 2 absorbed by the blocker via trample assignment)" into an opponent at 30 — verified kill. 002: opponents at 24 and 20 — verified damage, not lethal. 005: both opponents carry note "unaffected". Grapeshot is in 002's scenario hand and its final_state hand at storm count 4 and is resolved by no stack. "exactly one of them is checker-passed as lethal" holds.

Gating scope holds and no wide phrasing survives. goldfish_targets.json marks only "Zada online with a cantrip drawn" commander: true; the other two carry no commander key. Scenario boards: 001 and 003 hold Zada, 002 is Impact Tremors + 4 Mountains, 005 is Storm-Kiln Artist + 3 tokens, 004's extras say "Zada, Hedron Grinder (in the command zone)". SPF[0] scopes itself explicitly ("a single point of failure for the deck's best plan, not for the deck"). The archetype's two commander-reading cards verify: Siege-Gang Lieutenant's clause is "if you control your commander" and War Room pays "life equal to the number of colors in your commanders' color identity". Also confirmed: bracket floor 4 with game_changers [] driven by Storm-Kiln Artist + Haze of Rage, and that driver sits on the ungated half.

The rescope works. "the only card that fetches a Goblin from the library straight onto the battlefield" survives the counterexamples: Goblin Lackey is from hand on damage, Conspicuous Snoop CASTS off the top, Goblin Matron fetches to hand, and Hidden Volcano / Daring Discovery cast via Discover rather than fetch — the entry draws the fetch/cast line explicitly and correctly. Every mechanical claim verifies: Moggcatcher is a Human Mercenary (so Goblin Warchief's "Goblin spells" reduction, Skirk Prospector's "Sacrifice a Goblin", and the three Goblin-death triggers all miss it) and 4 + {3} = seven mana across two turns. The cut list also has a genuine `painful` entry (cut_candidates[4]) rather than dodging one, and validate-diagnosis computed orphans_stack null correctly — I cross-checked all five cut names against all five passing stacks' scenario blocks and none appears.

Correctly stated and correctly routed to gaps rather than silently fixed. strategic_frame.json's engines[0] does list Great Train Heist among Zada's cantrips, verbatim. Its Spree modes are "Untap all creatures you control" (no target), "Creatures you control get +1/+0 and gain first strike" (no target) and "Choose target opponent" — none targets a creature, so no configuration makes it target only Zada and the copy trigger cannot fire. It is a card read, as the entry says. gaps[3] also verifies: both quoted frame gap strings are present verbatim and both named sections now resolve. gaps[5] verifies: I queried the strategy DB and grepped strategy.md — no section mentions shroud or a self-targeting commander. gaps[0] verifies: no artifact in data/ carries per-commander inclusion rates (cards.csv has only a global edhrec_rank).

"the only pool line that both deepens the thinnest gated component and would add a second verified kill" holds. combo_details.json records ['Zada, Hedron Grinder', 'Storm-Kiln Artist', 'Seething Anger'] at popularity 664 as claimed. Across the 38 distinct in-identity pool cards that complete a line one card away from this decklist, Seething Anger is the only instant or sorcery targeting a single creature — the others that target a creature (Fall of Cair Andros, Thousand-Year Elixir, Staff of Domination, The Fire Crystal, Gimli's Reckless Might, Barbarian Class) are enchantments or artifacts, which Zada does not copy. Correctly held as "needs a stack scenario" rather than asserted, as are the Reiterate and Birgi lines.

Freshness is clean, so no figure here is stale. deck-audit's freshness block reports goldfish_metrics.json and mana_analysis.json both current against decklist_sha256 c8c1c7dd..., which matches the diagnosis header and cards.json. I re-derived every quoted figure against the live artifacts: 36 lands / 15 entries, 41 sources vs Burgess 31+1+4=36, 43 red sources / 69 red pips vs Karsten's 36, 15 ramp with 6 ramp:ritual, 8 card-advantage, 13 interaction, 0 sweepers, 2 protection, 2 threat-density, 27 creatures, breadth 2, 0.9 turn-3 land drop vs a 0.74 floor, 79.1% keep-first-seven, modal MV 2 with 19 two-drops / 13 three-drops / one card at MV 8+ (Blasphemous Act at 9), bracket floor 4, 2 tutors, component sizes 6/5/2/4, rates 0.661 / 0.6 / 0.152 and by-turn-6 0.496 / 0.487 / 0.091. All match. Every citation in the document is verbatim in its section, and the two most quotable traps are avoided: the Command Zone ratios are used with the aggro override named (34-36) rather than as a rule, and the strategy:deckbuilding.ratios "counts of functions, not cards" caveat is honoured at the ramp axis. One nit not worth a finding: axes[2]'s "5 unconditional taplands plus 3 conditional" mirrors mana_analysis.json's enters_tapped_always=5 / enters_tapped=8, but Den of the Bugbear enters tapped only "if you control two or more other lands", so the true split is 4 + 4. The artifact's heuristic, not the doctor's read, and the axis verdict is unaffected.

skeptic.note:
DIAGNOSE_MAX_ITERATIONS reached with seven findings open of seventeen. The re-grounding VERIFIED GOOD: the interaction-suite quote is verbatim, the invented commander-dependence premise is gone from all three sites, and the one-slot arithmetic holds (1 effective < 2, and 1+1 equals the lower band's floor exactly). All six of the doctor's own sweep fixes hold too.

The load-bearing failure is an INVERTED FIGURE. `axes[10]` and `add_candidates[3]` say 'mean bodies 2.698 on turn 4, so an early cantrip copies fewer than twice'. Zada copies for each OTHER creature, and `goldfish.py:build_library` drops commanders from the library, so 2.698 already excludes her -- it is ~2.7 copies, MORE than twice. Proved from inside the artifact: turn 3 is 2.355 and turn 4 is 2.698, a rise of 0.343, smaller than the 0.7002 the commander alone would add. Do not quote that 'fewer than twice' reading.

Five of the remaining six are scoping fixes and the adds and cuts survive them. Not blessed: `deck-diagnosis` stays MISS.
